scope: KEY: the delta decoder handles exactly ONE mode operation per entity per snapshot, and mode 1 reads its three position components INLINE - so a single mode-1 delta positions an entity
the_exit_0x671a0d: it loads a list head from [0x77D8218], walks it comparing [edi+0x18] (the entity id), and finally sets a bit in a bitset at [0x77D821C] using id>>3 and 1<<(id&7)
that is a 'mark this entity as changed' bookkeeping step, then it returns
so 0x671700 processes ONE mode operation and returns - it does not loop over further operations
the_consequence_for_sequences: modes 3 and 4 only set the stream scratch fields [+0x24] and [+0x28]; mode 1 and mode 8 read them
since each snapshot carries one operation, a mode-3-then-mode-1 sequence would have to be spread across TWO snapshots
but that is only needed for the fields at [edi+0x10] and [edi+8]
why_mode_1_alone_is_enough_for_a_positio: the three position components are read INLINE by 0x6715D0, 0x6714D0 and 0x671550 from the bit stream, not from scratch
0x6715D0 reads gate, scale and a 5-bit value and produces a float
so mode 1, by itself, supplies everything needed to write [edi+0x24], [edi+0x2C] and [edi+0x28]
the scratch-based fields ([edi+0x10], [edi+8]) would be zero, but the entity would still have a real position
